data.leadership_messages:
Our Proactive Partnership has benefited from schedule development as we consistently collaborate with our Northrop counterparts as they build BOEs, schedules, and other artifacts, allowing us to ensure a common understanding of portfolio scope and discuss concerns.
While we are evaluating what we can for BOEs and schedules, these are still in development and missing durations, logic, etc. Anticipating rework as we evaluate products that are still being updated.

There is pressure to create an aggressive schedule to meet IOC dates, and our concern is that logic or durations may be optimistic rather than realistic to show an ability to meet key milestones.
data.rationale: Have moderate confidence in the planning foundation for development of schedule artifacts. Transparency and a solid relationship will enable collaborative discussions, but schedules in previous years that were missing key logic or scope left us with some definite concerns that we’ll be looking for in future evaluations.

In reviewing initial drafts of BOEs and schedules, our team has moderate confidence that the new scope and deliverables are captured. However, with the schedule being largely in planning packages, it can be difficult to see the level of detail required to confirm the full scope is captured at this early stage.

data.products: Draft Schedule: Met with Northrop and reviewed their WBS for LSA. We have a regular monthly cadence for Shoulder-to-Shoulder reviews to discuss schedule and EVM data. We talked through our expectations for logic and durations as well as our concerns.
data.strengths:
Our teams are embedded, which allows us to discuss concerns and understand progress as artifacts are being developed. We also have confidence that our Northrop counterparts understand the scope based on working collaboratively together
which was demonstrated through our efforts on the Product Support Analysis Plan (PSAP).
data.concerns: Concern that logic ties will be missing, so we’ll be evaluating future schedules for that logic. We are also concerned about overly optimistic durations and/or lack of logic given the pressure to create a schedule that meets the overarching Level 1-3 schedule milestones.

4. Concerns and Risks Observed
Document the most significant concerns identified during the assessment and any associated risks that could reduce confidence in the contractor's planning maturity and readiness or adversely affect future planning, integration, or program execution if not addressed.
Concerns should be supported by objective evidence and identify observed weaknesses, gaps, inconsistencies, or uncertainties that warrant additional management attention. Risks should describe the potential consequences if those concerns remain unresolved.
Not every concern creates a program risk, and not every identified risk is currently affecting program execution. The purpose of this section is to identify issues that warrant Government visibility, follow-up, or corrective action as planning continues to mature.
Definitions
Concern: An observed weakness, gap, inconsistency, or uncertainty that may reduce confidence in the contractor's planning maturity and readiness.
Risk: A potential future consequence that could adversely affect planning, cost, schedule, technical performance, integration, PMB implementation, or program execution if a concern is not addressed.
Concern that logic ties will be missing, so we’ll be evaluating future schedules for that logic. We are also concerned about overly optimistic durations and/or lack of logic given the pressure to create a schedule that meets the overarching Level 1-3 schedule milestones.
5. Open Questions and Follow-Up Items
Document questions that remain unanswered during the assessment and identify the additional evidence, clarification, documentation, or demonstrations needed from the contractor to complete the evaluation or increase confidence in the assessment findings.
Open Questions and Follow-Up Items identify areas where the available evidence was incomplete, unclear, or inconsistent. These items represent information gaps that should be resolved through additional discussions, demonstrations, or artifact reviews before the Government can fully assess the contractor's planning maturity and readiness. They are not, by themselves, concerns, deficiencies, or risks.
